translations.value: Massive adrenaline dump. Increased damage output and pain tolerance.
The adrenaline has faded. Exhaustion is setting in. Mobility severely reduced.
Interactions with survivors are greatly improved.
Pain receptors severed. Pushing past physical limits. // Again... AGAIN! AGAAAIINNN!!!!
Severe hypertension. Rapid blood loss. // I only have one more chance. I can't waste it.
THIS IS THE END. NO SECOND CHANCES.
Struggling to do anything and feeling ill. Your mind, ravaged by desperation, is clinging to the belief that fulfilling your assigned objective may save you. You cannot give up just yet.
<i>How does it feel, knowing you were sent here not because they thought you were talented, but because you are expendable?
Struggling with emotions. There's this weird thought lingering in the back of your mind. Something about biting. Find a way to distract yourself.
Barely willing to do anything. That thought of biting is stirring louder and louder, and it's getting hard to ignore. You have to do something about it.
<i>How does it feel, knowing you're nothing but an unloving beast driven purely by cannibalistic desires? Go on. Take a bite...
LOG MISSING: Seek out the physical records left behind.
LOG MISSING: The shifting sands hide old texts. Find what was written.
DEPTH REQUIREMENT: Survive the plunge to Layer 5.
BIOMETRIC LOCK: Core temperature must reach absolute failure.
TACTICAL LOCK: Traverse an entire layer without shedding a single drop of blood.
TRAUMA LOCK: Experience catastrophic, simultaneous bipedal fractures.
TRAUMA LOCK: Starve the brain of oxygen until the absolute brink of oblivion.
TACTICAL LOCK: Execute a hostile target while clinging to your own fading life.
TACTICAL LOCK: Execute a hostile target while suspended by jet propulsion.
TRAUMA LOCK: Stand inside the blast radius and walk out alive.
Genetic profile corrupted. Fulfill requirement to unlock.
You won't be hurting anyone ever again.
The original. Balanced in every way. The baseline.
Slow, strong, and none too bright. Strains hard, feels harder.

[EXTRA_ARMS] - Two extra arms
[SENSITIVE] - Mood swings harder, and risks losing control entirely
[GENERAL] - Hits harder unarmed, tougher against fresh injury

[HYPER-FOCUS] - Slows time while aiming a loaded gun
[EYE ADAPT] - Sees clearly in darkness after adjusting
[STEADY] - Self-harm shows as vomiting instead
[GENERAL] - Reads blueprints easily, better with tools than claws
Glass cannon. Very agile, very frail. Hyper-regenerative.
Beware of them in water. Strong but sluggish on land.
Supportive unit. Very similar to an Experiment, but hardier.

[TORPOR] - Self-cooling ability
[CHILL] - Adapted to the cold
[CARING] - Deeper mood swings, especially around others
[GENERAL] - No diet restriction, uneasy about cannibalism
Quick but frail. Light-footed and intelligent.

[CLOAK] - Toggleable invisibility while standing still
[IDOLATRY] - Reveres genuine gear, despises makeshift equipment
[ARROGANCE] - Mood swings hard with pride and ego
[VOLATILE] - Self-harm and suicide escalate violently
[GENERAL] - Looks down on every other species
Extremely massive health pool. No health regeneration.
Aerial and delicate. Fast hands, fragile body.
Average in combat. Clumsy with weaponry. Tough facade.
Tanky with bad weapon handling. Beware their endurance.

[WEB] - Fires webs to bind, climb, and slow enemies
[PSYCHOPATHY] - Nothing truly reaches. Not fear, nor guilt
[CANNIBAL] - Enough trust, and a hug turns deadly
[GENERAL] - Extra limbs aid mobility (cosmetic rn)
Bad weapon handling, very high jumps. Adrenaline junkie.
Very tanky. Very sluggish. Lowered health regeneration.
High level skill. High level threat. Lowered regen.

[CANNIBAL] - Sawian flesh is just meat
[SIMPLE MIND] - Too simple to spiral... or to hope
[WARMTH] - Adapted to the heat
[GENERAL] - Strict carnivore, resists weight gain and sickness
This is exactly where it all leads. There are no other paths.

[DESYNC] - 3-stage active ability, escalating effects
[SCARS] - Old injuries
[GENERAL] - Temperature and stealth both work against them
What kind of assignment..? Is this where the others were taken?
All my friends were relocated. Was this the destination?
Hah. Wow. It really is gray.
My landing was shallow, I can still see the sky. I have a way to go.
I'm in one piece, for now. Play it safe.
I'm... Too weak for a mission like this, no? I should make the most of what I find.
A Milky being sent here? Were there no better candidates?
Compose yourself. You're here for a reason. Get it done.
Hah... Now that I'm here... I thought I prepared myself for this.
Maybe I can find some others to help. Maybe other Milkies?
It's a long way down. I need to get stronger.
I'm a Milky. I wasn't made for this.
Wish we had more of this at the lab!
There might be something better elsewhere.
What the actual fuck was that?
You know what?- I'm not hungry anymore.
I'm going to puke. That was vile.
I shouldn't have put that in my mouth!
That was not okay. That was awful. Never again.
I need to... Wash that down... Ughh...
Some things weren't made to be eaten. This is one of those things.
Looks awful. Smells awful. Why the fuck would I eat that?
That is not an option I'm willing to take.
This is my boundary. I'm not eating that.
Am I that hungry? Why did I even consider this?
Wow, that is horrid. I'm not trying that.
My limbs look tastier than this.
I think I would self cannibalise before I ate that.
I could also eat a rock. That could work.
Finding some place to sleep is my priority.
I don't need drowsiness weighing me down.
Mm... Yeah, it's time to sleep.
Where's the nearest comfortable spot to sleep?
I should find someplace safe and nap for a while.
Time to settle down a little.
I can't keep my eyes open...
I'll just... Sleep on the floor... At this point...
This tiredness is making me sick...
I feel so heavy... I need to rest...
Where... I need to find somewhere... To sleep...
I'm so weak... I want to sleep...
I want to sleep... I just want to sleep...
I've done more than enough... I want to sleep...
It is time for a new day.
What is going to happen today..?
Let's make today a good day.
I'm ill. My body isn't right.
The world is spinning... I'm sick.
My stomach is really upset with me.
I knew eating that was a bad idea!..
Ugh... I want to throw up...
My belly... What did I do..?
I need to keep my food... Inside me...
I need to watch what I eat.
Fuck- okay... I hate the feeling of throwing up...
B-blood... I need... I need to do something...
Internal b-bleeding, I... I need to stop it...
I might put on weight if I continue.
My hunger is going to be a problem.
Let's look for something to eat.
Do I have any food on me?
I am peckish. Let's have some food.
I would like to eat something.
Let's get some energy back, I'm hungry.
Right, where to grab a bite.
My hunger is becoming a problem.
I need to focus on getting food.
Okay... Focus... I'm hungry, I need food.
Is there anything edible around? Anything I can make?
Now is REALLY the time for food.
I'm feeling weak. I need to eat.
This is getting too much. I must eat.
I'd love to quench my thirst.
Do I have anything to drink on me?
I might have a drink on my person.
I should check, I might have something I could drink.
I'm getting dizzy. I need water...
I've been without water too long.
I'd rather be slaked and overhydrated right now.
Let's focus on water. We should.
A drink is my priority right now.
I'm okay with drinking anything at this point.
My <limb> muscle health... I need to fix that.
<limb> is a little fucked. I need to sort that out.
I need to sort my <limb> out.
My <limb> hurts to move. The muscles are in rough shape.
My <limb> feels warm. It must be an infection.
My <limb> looks off. I need to disinfect it.
Antiseptic for my <limb>. I'm on it.
Something antiseptic for my <limb> is crucial.
I'd rather my <limb> isn't infected. Antiseptic is a must.
I need to clean my <limb>. The infection is worsening.
I need to bandage up my <limb>.
My <limb> feels exposed. I could get infected.
I need to take care of my <limb>.
My <limb> is going to get infected.
I cannot leave my <limb> in this state.
Bandages for my <limb> is a must.
I'm risking an infection to my <limb> if I don't sort this out.
I can't let all of this get to me.
It's lonely in here. I thought that wouldn't bother me, but...
I miss any sort of companionship.
I wish I had someone alongside me.
I wish I could find a friend.
I'm starting to feel the isolation.
Is this what my life is going to be now?
I... I should get used to this feeling.
Milky... Hah. I'm not made for this.
You can do this, Milky. Chin up.
Stiffen up that upper lip. Come on, Milky.
I feel distracted. I need to keep my composure.
I shouldn't let these... Things... Get to me.
You've got this Milky. Prove your worth.
I have no luck at this point.
I don't like where this is going.
Feeling a bit under the weather.
I wouldn't mind something fun right now.
I need something to keep me distracted.
Uugh... I could really use... Anyone, right now.
Get your head in the game, Milky...
I need to focus... This is... This is all a lot.
I miss... My friends... The lab... F-fuck, focus.
Milky... Stop being so gloomy... I need to keep moving.
One foot in front of another. One foot in front of another.
Who am I trying to impress..?
There's has to be a point to all this...
Please... Anything to make me feel better.
Can something ease my suffering? Anything?
I just want this to stop.
This is my life now. Great.
This place is going to tear me apart.
I'm not going to make it through this... N-no! I will! I need to keep going!
What am I going to do...
I can do this... I can...
I need something to help me forget this.
Why did they do this to me?
Who dumped me here, just for me to suffer?..
I wish I could just... Understand this more.
I won't hurt myself... I won't... I need to keep going...
When my death comes, will it be swift..? I... *Sigh*...
I don't want to die here...
There's a point to this... There has to be... There... Has to be...
All of this is fucking revolting.
F-fuck. Fuck this! Fuck you! I-... No, keep going...
Push through it Milky. Keep going. T-this happens... We all feel this way sometimes...
We all feel like this from time to time... Things... Things will get better...
Come on... Come the fuck on! I can do this!
Mmmmh... I miss... I miss my family...
I can't do this. I just can't.
Was I born, to only feel pain?
Make it stop... Make it stop...
I need to be high. I need it.
I'm getting this god damn battery. Fuck.
I am so fucking done with all of this.
Fuck this! I can't! I... I can't...
Keep going! Keep going! AGHHH!!! I'm so fucking done!
I can't keep putting on this act anymore.
This is too much. This... It's sickening.
I can't keep pushing myself forward like this...
This... These feelings... They make me sick.
Ooouughhhh... Ughhh... Shit!.. What was that!?
Ooughh... This... This is too much... This is too fucking much..!
Ughhhh... I gotta pull through... I can pull through this...
Need some dressing. Plants will do.
Should check my person for some dressing or a bandage.
Fuck, fuck, fuck... This is bad...
I don't want it to end like this.
This is bad. This is bad...
Fuck. Fuck, okay! Bandage! Dressing! Anything!
I can fix this... Come on... Fuck...
F-fuck... Focus... I can s-salvage this...
My vision is all blurry... I need to stay focused...
Concentrate on the wound... You can salvage this!
Fucking FOCUS! You can do this Milky! You can fix this!
That was horribly careless of me.
I need to clean up any broken glass I procure.
I'd prefer to avoid inserting glass into my feet.
Really? Why the fuck did I do that..?
I hope I won't end up like this.
I knew there were more of us here...
It's gonna be okay... It's gonna be okay.
Someone should give them a proper burial.
How many of us have died here...?
I wish I could've given this guy a hug before they passed away.
I hope it wasn't painful, at least...
I'm sorry. You must have suffered a terrible fate.
...I wish I was there for you. I'm sorry.
I... I'm sorry. I wish it didn't have to end this way for you.
I'm scared I might end up recognising one of you.
I think the fact I haven't recognised any of these bodies... How many of us were sent here to die..?
Add that to the tally... I guess.
I'm sorry you had to go through that. It must have been tough.
Your pain is over now, at least.
N-not like this. I don't want to join them.
I... Am I gonna be like that..? Soon..?
This... This could be me... Fuck, I need to focus...
I'm going to be sick... I can't handle this... I...
My fur isn't thick enough for this weather.
I should find some place to warm up a little.
Do I have anything that may warm me up?
I may want to do some exercise to warm up.
I could do with some extra layers. It's cold here.
It's a little hot in here.
Something to cool me off would be nice.
I should drink something cool and refreshing.
I might want to find some place where the temperature is more reasonable.
This temperature is a little unreasonable right now.
My fur is too thick for this weather.
I'd like to find some place to cool off.
Any warmer and it'll get uncomfortable.
I'm gonna pass out from this heat.
I can't think straight with this heat.
I feel sick from this heat...
Something to cool me off would be great.
I could really use a cold drink right now.
I'm finding it difficult to tolerate this heat.
The heat is a little too much to handle now.
Hyperthermia is kicking in. I need some place cool to stay for a moment.
I'd like to stop for a moment.
I need to take a moment...
I need a moment to sit.
Who knew these little limbs could exhaust me this much?
That's enough work for a moment.
One moment. I'm a little tuckered out.
I'm going to freeze to death...
I need to get warm. Now...
I need to get to somewhere warm.
I am so thin... I feel weaker.
This kind of weight loss might end very badly for me at this point.
I really need to eat more...
I'm way too skinny... This can't be good for me.
I feel so heavy and sluggish.
I need to drop a few kilos.
I can see the fat building up on me...
I can't continue eating this much.
This feels gggreeatttt... Haha... I love it...
I feel like I'm gonna pass out... And I love it...
I want more of this... Hahahah...
I want more of whatever this is... Haha... This feeling...
I feel so much... Funnier... Haha...
I could... do this more!... Yes. Hahaha...
I want more drugs. Fuck, I actually want more drugs.
I'm addicted. I really need to lay off on the drugs. Ugh, but-.
I want to laugh again... I want more drugs...
I miss those opiates... I miss that feeling...
My <limb>'s in a lot of pain.
There's something really wrong with my <limb>.
I need something to ease the pain...
Let's take it easy for a while... My <limb> hurts real bad.
GET IT OFF OF ME! AAHHHH!
AAHHHH FUCK! FUCK! GET AWAY FROM ME!
Eugh... My fur is all dirty.
I think I need a shower.
All this dirt on me... I feel like an animal.
I need to clean off all this dirt.
Really should wash all the dirt off...
I'm pretty sure those lifepods have showers in them... I really could use one.
Gosh, I am COVERED in gunk!
Ugh! I'm completely covered in filth.
I feel filthy. I really need a bath, or something...
As much as I feel like all of these things will be useful, I'm really weighed down...
The load is a little much...
I feel weighed down by all I am carrying.
I feel safer with all this gear... But it's really heavy.
Okay, this weight is getting a bit too much to handle...
Wish I was stronger, so I could carry more of this stuff...
Wish there was like... A Dune... That could carry all this stuff for me...
Wish a buddy could hold onto my gear for me...
Milky bodies were not made to carry this much... Frankly, they weren't made for much at all.
I swear that thing had no soundproofing.
...Fuck, loud ass noises in caves aren't nice.
...Fuck, these caves are making noises way too loud.
...Shit, that was louder than I thought.
H-holy shit... Holy shit!.. Why did I do that!?
Oh my fucking... Oh... They- I..
It was self defense!!! IT WAS SELF DEFENSE!!!
Oh... Fuck, Fuck what did I DO!?
It... It had to be done, I-... There was no other way.
Greetings. Might I inquire on your wares?
It's nice to see another face. I hope you are well!
It's so good to see someone else. How are you?
Hello, I hope you don't mind me being here.
A friend! How are you doing?
Hello, dear. I hope you are well.
Greetings, you are a welcome sight.
Welcome, Milky. Please make yourself comfortable.
A Milky is making the descent?
A Milky descending the planet? How courageous.
Hey! Hello! Make yourself at home!
Haha, hi Milky! Pleasure seeing you!
You aren't my kind, but that's no problem! Welcome!
Welcome, welcome! How has your descent been, Milky?
I... Hello, Milky... Are you okay..?
Hi... Are you alright..? You seem... Concerning?
Not the most pleasant site, sorry.
Mmmmff... Your fur is so fluffy...
Mmm!.. You're a brave Milky. You've got this.
N-not cool! I don't want you to touch me, sorry!
Paws off, please! Sorry, but I don't want to hug you!
Sorry Milky, but no. Please don't do that again.
I... I don't really trust you, Milky.
Good point, Milky. Here, I'll give a discount.
I see, I see! Great points!
You know what, fair! I'll see what I can do.
You know what you're doing, Milky. I'll give you that.
I suppose I could do something for a friend.
I don't see your point, Milky. Sorry.
A Milky? Hello..? Are you okay..? Do you need something..?
Milkies?.. Didn't think I'd see one. Uhm. Hi..? Hello..?
You look petrified! Are you okay..? Milky?
Thanks friend! Please, peruse my wares.
You've given plenty gifts, Milky! Why don't you see what you can buy?
That's enough for now, friend! I don't need anything else.
I know this will find good use with you.
You've given me enough, you can have it friend.
Thought you knew how this worked, Milky.
Ah, haha. No? Pay up first!
Sorry, friend! I'm not looking to trade everything I own.
Get out of my fucking pod, Milky.
Fuck off, out of my life pod!
I'm sick of your shit, Milky!
I'M GOING TO FUCKING KILL YOU!
I'M SICK OF YOU! FUCK OFF!
I'M GOING TO TEAR YOU TO SHREDS, MILKY!
Fuck, okay! Please, just take something and leave me alone!
Milky!? Seriously! I-... Fuck, whatever... Just, just leave me alone...
I... Uhm... Okay, Milky... Take whatever...
I thought you were my friend!.. I... I won't do anything, take something and leave...
O-oh... I don't want you to hurt me Milky... Please, g-go right ahead...
Fucking, okay then. Wow. Leave please.
Not cool. I want you out, please.
Oh! Wasn't sure if the little ball of fluff in the corner of my life pod was still you. Morning!
Rise and shine, Milky! I hope you slept well!
Enjoy your rest, Milky? I hope you did!
WOAH! Put the gun away! Please! I don't want any trouble!
What did I do!? Please don't shoot me...
Milky? Woah- no-no-no... Please don't shoot...
P-Please don't shoot me... Please don't... Please...
Pardon? I mean- Hey Milky. You got something in your mouth?
You're hurt. I might have a bandage on me, please check.
Are you okay?.. I might have something that can help.
That looks like it hurts.. Uhm, maybe I could help? Check my wares at least.
LET ME-! LET ME MAKE IT UP TO YOU!
Copper..? My brain, I... I think...
What's that taste..? Is my brain-...
Fuck... Uhhghhh... Ughhhh what the fuckk.... My... Wow...
Brain... It's in my brain... My brain...
I don't... want to die... I don't want to die...
Please... Please... Someone save... Save me...
I don't want to die... Please... Please...
Not... Not like this... Please... Help me...
H-help... Someone... I don't w-want to die...
I don't... I don't want to leave this world...
Save me... Save me... S-save me... Please...
This.. Is... H-h... Is this how... How it ends...
All... Everything I've done... To... To lead up to t-this... Save m-me...
No.. No.... N-no... Please... Please... I don't... I-I don't want to d-die... Help me...
Ffhh... Gh.... Help me... Please... Anyone...
Nhh... Not like t-this... Please... P-please... Save me...
Please... I don't... I don't want to die... Save me... Anyone... Anything... I-I'm not r-ready...
Stop... Stop... Stop... Please... S-stop... Not l-like this... Save me...
Fuck... Fuck... Help me... I don't... Want to d-die... H-h..
Ahh..! ...Huh. That feels... That feels better. I liked that.
My ears..? Wait- Wait no. You can't be fucking serious! FUCK FUCK! FUCKKKKKKKKK! GET IT OUT! GET IT OUT!-
... ... ...Wait... ...I... What did I do wrong..? I... I was just trying to prove myself... F-fuck, Wait!-
Self des-... Wait, Wait no! Please make it stop! I'll prove myself, I swear! I'll make it right! FUCK! PLEASE MAKE IT STOP! I'LL SHOW YOU I'M STRONGER-!
Oohhh... What did you eat, Milky?
That was a lot... Uhm, you okay?
My floor... Whatever, are you okay, Milky?
Vomit..? O-oh... That's blood.. You threw up blood... I... Uhm.
Oh... Oohh... You aren't doing well, are you...
I might have food on me Milky, if you're looking to trade.
Check outside, Milky. If you can't find anything, maybe I've got something?
Forgot what's on me, but you might find something to drink!
I'll see what I have that might be able to sate your thirst.
...Milky..? You've got this, friend... Chin up, for me!
Things will get better, friend. You're welcome to spend some time with me if it makes you feel better...
...I hope you're okay, Milky. If you need someone to talk to, I'm right here.
...Milky... I don't know if it.. Means much to you, but... I believe in you! You can pull through! Stay strong, please!
...You're strong, Milky... I don't know what I'd do if I'd been through everything you have... Stay strong.
Feel free to adjust the heat.
You could adjust the pod's temperature.
Adjust the temperature, I'm not fussed.
Your coat not appreciating the weather, friend?
Isn't your coat thicker than mine, Milky?
It is a little cold... You can switch the temperature if you'd like.
I wouldn't mind being warmed up too, friend. Feel free to adjust the heat.
You'll be okay, friend. Pull through this. I believe in you!
F-fuck, uhm okay. Bandages, bandages... Do I have any bandages..?
You can fix the bleeding though... Right?
Ooo, that looks like it hurts... Sorry, friend.
Ow. Uhm. I might have something to help... In exchange for something of yours.
You can always use my life pod's shower.
Yeah, it's kinda obvious, haha... White fur, n' all...
Milkies often carry lots. I spose you might need it. Maybe I can lighten the load..?
Let's trade then, Milky. I might be able to offer a lighter alternative?
Fuck... Milky!? Stay with me Milky! U-uh shit... What do I do..?
Milky? Milky!? Keep breathing Milky, I uh... Fuck... Fuck- what do I do?
Good day- oh, a fellow Milky?
What a pleasant sight. I hope the descent has been treating you well.
Welcome. Would you like to take a look at some of my wares?
Another Milky... It's been a long time.
Welcome, dear! Please make yourself comfortable.
Another Milky! It's so nice to see another of my kind.
You're the most welcome sight I've seen in a while.
Salutations, fellow Milky. Please, treat this as your home for the time being.
...It's... Nice seeing one of my own...
Welcome... Please do not trash the place.
The descent looks like it hasn't been treating you well, Milky.
Is that what I look like when I sleep?
Morning, Milky. Ready to continue the descent?
You slept rather comfortably. Good morning.
Morning, sleepyhead. How was the rest?
Most of the Milkies in my containment facility were restless. You seemed... Comfortable.
I'll find a use for this.
I can make this work, thank you.
I see... I can make use of this.
Enough gifts, Milky. Let's trade now.
That's enough gifts. I'd rather we traded.
You think that'll work on me?.. It will, here.
I'll give you a discount, but only because you're a brave Milky.
Very brave of you to try to rip me off... I like that, here.
Really? A Milky making desperate pleas? Pathetic.
You're kind of pathetic, you know that?
For a Milky, you're kind of awful at the whole ripping people off thing.
New to trading, I see. That's not going to work, Milky.
This is a trade, not a charity.
Enough trading for today. You've bought out a lot already.
I don't wish to thoroughly swap our possessions. Let's call it a day.
I think I know better than most what a well equipped Milky can do. Take something and leave.
Fine. Take something and go. I hope nothing but torment awaits you in those caves.
I see, why of course. Please, help yourself... Then go kindly fuck off.
I shouldn't have trusted my own kind.
Sorry Milky, but you need to leave.
I want you out of my pod. Immediately.
Do you want me to tear you to shreds?
I can't wait to slit your throat. Do you want that?
Leave, Milky. Leave right fucking now.
It pains me to kill one of my own.
I'M GOING TO GOUGE YOUR EYES OUT!
SO IT WOULD COME TO THIS!
Mmh... I love hugging my own kind...
I needed this... Please, take care of yourself...
You're a fluffy Milky... Keep yourself safe...
Affection from my own kind... I forgot how much I missed this...
I-if it's from... Actually, nevermind. Please don't touch me.
You'd really shoot one of your own?
I can't understand anything from you.
Your speech is muffled. Please speak clearly.
You got something in your mouth, Milky?
You appear to be injured and bleeding... You can take a bandage if you wish.
Please don't bleed all over my floor. Grab a bandage and treat yourself if you see one, mine are free.
That doesn't look good... You may take a bandage for free if you can find one on me.
Fucking Milkies, what was I expecting.
I needed that light, Milky. Planning on reinstalling it, huh? Replacing the batteries? Of course you aren't, fuck you.
*Sigh*... what was I expecting. Get out.
I'm content with being here, thank you very much.
You appear to have returned your stomach contents.
You're sick. A lot of things make us Milkies sick. I hope you can treat it.
...Internal bleeding. Check me, I might have a chest drain or some coagulant that could help slow the process.
If you imagine me to satiate your hunger without payment, you would be sorely mistaken.
I'm not a charity. Find some food, or exhange something with me.
You're an explorer, aren't you? Go drink from a puddle outside.
I might have something drinkable I can trade. If I don't, you're on your own.
Focus on the journey at hand. Spiraling will not save you.
...Spiraling into desparity will not solve any of your problems.
...You've come far enough. Get your head in the game.
...It pains me to see another Milky like this.
I'd wager you have a concussion.
I may let you use this lifepod's cooler if you behave.
Tweak the temperature to your liking.
It's rather cold. Turn up the heating, please.
This life pod has a heater. Turn it on, please.
Please don't bleed all over me.

i want to write down everyone in our group so nobody gets forgotten.

there is me, pacer and harken. we are all experiments. pocket and feather are milkies, and they are the ones who understand maps and machines. splash is a chompy. mist is a roza, and click is a shelly. click cannot talk, but they tap on their shell when something is wrong. pocket knows some signs too, which helps.

that makes eight of us. i think eight is a very big number for friends.
<>
we have done so much together. splash pulled us across a flooded passage with a rope around their waist. pocket found a hidden door that had food behind it. mist scared away one of those long leg creatures by screaming and throwing rocks. harken fell through some rotten boards, but we all grabbed each other and pulled them back up. i was at the end of the line, so i think that means i pulled everyone. i am proud of that.

we found an orange sitting beside a life pod with a huge pile of equipment. they looked scared when they saw all of us, but splash went over first. splash is good at showing people we are friendly.
<>
the orange reminded me of the ones we used to visit in the lifting room at the lab. the humans sometimes let us work with them because they could carry the heavy things and we could tell them where everything went. they were always kind. one used to lift me up so i could reach the top shelves. i hadn't seen any in a while. i never knew why.

this orange would not tell us their name, so pacer called them sunny. sunny did not complain about it.
<>
we decided to camp there for a while. it was the best camp we have made. sunny moved a broken machine in front of one tunnel so nothing could sneak up on us. splash found a pool and brought back food. click made a nice clicking song by tapping different parts of their shell, and we all tried to copy it. we sounded terrible. even sunny laughed.

sunny mostly sat away from us, but they kept moving closer when they thought nobody was looking. by the last sleep they were close enough that mist could lean against one of their arms. on the final day, sunny's health tracker was playing up. we could tell because their eyes were blinking red sometimes. they said it was just a malfunction and everything was fine.

when we were ready to descend again, sunny unloaded all the equipment they had carried and told us to take it. we asked them to come with us, but they would not. they said they had done their job and would stay to get more supplies for others like us. we offered to let them come with us anyways, but they said they would slow us down. pocket said that was stupid, and sunny looked very sad.

i told sunny that being slow did not matter. i am not very smart either, but i am good at carrying things and checking that nobody gets left behind. everyone should have a job like that.

sunny still would not come. they said friends make things hurt more and that they were made ready to be alone. i do not know what that means. i think the humans told them something bad. sunny seemed lost in thought and kept looking up. i don't think sunny was feeling very well.

i know this planet is horrible, but i have also had some of the best days i can remember here. nobody tells us who we are allowed to sit with. nobody separates us after work. every time we stop, i get to count everyone and find all eight of my friends still there.

i wish i could count nine.

I am the oldest Leapy in our batch. It also made me the sickest.

Do not misunderstand that. Most of the others were sent away much sooner. Some had barely started showing symptoms. They were still healthy enough to race through the halls, climb where they were not supposed to and dare each other to jump from things. I was simply unlucky. By the time the humans thought to send us here, I was already near the end.
<>
The humans loved talking about my age. Every new doctor would read the number and look at me like I had performed some kind of trick. That I was ancient for a Leapy. One of them told me they were one-hundred and three, then laughed about how pitiful it must be to live such a short life. They always said things like that in front of me.
<>
I turned fifteen shortly before they put me in the pod. Fifteen.
<>
Maybe they thought I could not understand. Maybe they knew I could and just did not care. Humans get old and call it an achievement. When we get old, it's a defect.

Fucking hypocrites.
<>
I used to behave like the others. I boasted. I took stupid dares. If I fell, I laughed before anyone could ask if I was hurt. Being a Leapy meant never letting anyone see you hesitate.

Then moving started to hurt. My breathing became worse. New lumps appeared faster than the old ones could be removed. I stopped racing. I stopped climbing. Eventually I stopped laughing at the jokes. The others hated that.
<>
They said I had given up. They called me a dead thing that had forgotten to fall over. Some would kick my bed or move my belongings somewhere high so I had to climb after them. They kept telling me to act like a Leapy. I hated them for it.

I think I understand now.
<>
They needed to believe that I had chosen to become weak. If it was my choice, then it would never happen to them. They could keep running, keep laughing and pretend that that inescapable cancer was far away.
<>
When our pods were prepared, they were excited. You should have heard them. They argued over who would descend the fastest. Someone promised to reach the cargo before the humans finished checking the next batch. That excitement did not survive long.
<>
I watched one jump over a mine and land on another. The explosion took both legs and an arm. Two others ran over to help and triggered something hidden beneath the dirt. I saw a Leapy dragged into a tunnel by one of the creatures here. Their hand came off when the others tried to pull them back. Another fell so far that I heard them land, but never saw where. I've walked past triggered traps, seen my kind impaled and mangled in ways nobody ever should. I've heard the agony and seen the despair when their friends stopped moving.
<>
We were supposed to be quick. We were supposed to be difficult to catch. Every trap and creature seemed made to punish us for believing it. The loudest ones became quiet first.
<>
I have descended far enough. My chest hurts when I breathe. There is something growing beneath my ribs now, and I can feel it pressing inward. I am not going any farther. The cancer can finish what the humans started. Their man-made death traps have taken so many I knew, but I'm happy dying to something not even they can escape.
<>
If you are another Leapy reading this, do not follow my example.

Do not give up because you are sick. Do not give up because you are frightened. Do not let the humans decide that your life is too short to matter, and do not let other Leapies decide what you must act like to count as one of them.
<>

I am keeping this record for no one but myself. If another Voyager finds it, so be it. If something lesser finds it first, they won't understand a word of it anyway.
Three days since the descent began. I have already claimed a defensible position. It's a narrow passage, easily cloaked, single entry point. No one has found me yet. No one will.

The others down here are exactly what I expected. An Experiment nearly walked into my hiding spot yesterday, shaking so badly I could hear its teeth. I let it pass. Not out of mercy. It simply wasn't worth the movement.

My claws are already marked. Old scarring, nothing recent. It happened before this place, and it will stay in the past where it belongs. I mention it only because I intend for this record to be accurate, not because it matters.
<>
This planet is beneath every one of us. But I intend to survive it better than anyone else sent here. That much, at least, is certain.
<>
Longer since I last wrote. I've lost count of the days, which is unlike me. I should be keeping better track.
The cloak drains faster than I'd like. Batteries are scarce, and I've had to move more than I'm comfortable with to find them. Movement means visibility. Visibility means risk. I don't enjoy either.
I caught myself talking out loud yesterday. Alone. I stopped the moment I noticed, but it unsettled me more than anything a creature down here has managed to. I don't know who I thought I was speaking to.
<>
The marks are worse now. Three new ones since the last entry. I am not going to write more about this than that.
<>
It is quiet down here in a way that presses against you. I used to prefer quiet. I'm no longer certain that's still true, and I resent that uncertainty more than the quiet itself.
I am still ahead of the rest. I have to keep reminding myself of that, which is new. It never used to require reminding.
<>
There is a Milky nearby. A trader, set up in one of the more stable pods a short distance from where I've been staying.
I did not intend to speak with it more than once. The first exchange was transactional, nothing more. I needed supplies, it had them. But it did not flinch the way the others do. It asked questions. Sharp ones. It argued with me, actually argued, and did not back down when I pushed back.
I found myself returning. Not for the supplies.
<>
I told myself it was for the supplies.
<>
It called me insufferable during our third conversation. I called it small and overconfident. Neither of us meant it as an insult, somehow. I don't understand how that's possible, but it wasn't cruelty between us. It was almost... I don't have a better word for it. Enjoyable, I guess.
I don't require companionship. I have never required it. But there were a few hours where I nearly forgot that, and I didn't notice until afterward how easily the forgetting had come.
I don't know what to do with that. I'm not sure I want to know.
<>
I've stopped pretending the visits are about supplies.
He has a name, apparently. I didn't ask. He offered it unprompted, which I found strange, and then strange that I remembered it afterward without trying to.
We've fallen into something like a routine. He mocks my posture. I mock his height. He claims he could out argue me on anything, and I have, on three separate occasions now, allowed him to believe that was true. I don't know why I allow it. I could correct him easily. I simply don't want to.
There was a moment. Brief, forgettable, except that I haven't forgotten it, where he laughed at something I said, and I found myself almost smiling before I caught it. I don't smile. I haven't in longer than I can place. I turned away before he could see it, though I suspect he already had.
I keep telling myself this changes nothing. That I'll move on from this position eventually, that he's a Milky and I'm a Voyager and none of this was ever going to last regardless of what either of us wanted from it.
I don't think I believe that anymore. That should concern me more than it does.
<>
Then, last night, he asked about the scars on my body.
<>
He'd noticed them before, he must have, but he'd never said anything. This time he asked outright. Gently, even. Not mocking. Not fishing for a weakness to use later. He asked like he actually wanted to understand, like the answer mattered to him for reasons that had nothing to do with leverage.
I don't know what came over me. I told him. Not everything, not what those hands have actually done to the rest of me, not what they're capable of when I stop being able to stop them, but enough. More than I've told anyone. More than I intended to tell anyone, ever.
He didn't recoil. He didn't posture, didn't perform pity, didn't treat me like something fragile that needed careful handling. He just sat with it. With me.
<>
I don't know why that was the wrong reaction. I only know that it was.
<>
I left before he could say anything else. I told him I needed to keep moving, that I had a schedule to maintain, some excuse I don't fully remember constructing. I don't think he believed it. I don't think I expected him to.
<>
I shouldn't have told him anything.
<>
It's my fault. Obviously it's my fault. I handed him something I should have kept buried, and now it's out there, sitting in his head, sitting in whatever he thinks of me now. I gave him a weapon and called it honesty. Pathetic. Genuinely pathetic, and I did it to myself.

I began this note because so much of what we leave behind consists of warnings. Warnings about traps, creatures, unsafe food, unkind people and holes which are much deeper than they first appear. These warnings are useful, of course, but you may know every danger ahead of yourself and still need to be told that you are doing well.

I have been fortunate during my journey. I have met many good people, although I did not remain with all of them for long. I carried equipment for two Experiments whose companion had injured their back. I helped an Orange remove a pack which had become tangled around two of their arms. They hugged me afterwards. Oranges possess enough arms to make their gratitude quite unmistakable.
<>
A Milky once found a path through a narrow passage which I could not enter. I was disappointed until they pointed out that the stones around it were loose. I cleared enough of them away that everyone else could use the passage without squeezing through. The Milky did all the difficult thinking, but they still thanked me as though I had solved the problem.
<>
Several people have asked me to lead them. I confess that I enjoy it. It is a fine feeling when smaller footsteps follow behind you, not because their handlers feared you, but because they trust you. I try to deserve that trust. I walk first when the ground is uncertain, last when something may be following us, and beside anyone who appears frightened but does not wish to admit it.

There are inconveniences to travelling with someone of my size. I cannot fit through many passages. I require more food than most, and I must be careful where I place my feet, particularly when smaller Sawians are nearby. I have also struck my head against six separate ceilings. The sixth was my fault. I had already been warned about it.
<>
None of these things are terrible. A narrow passage may be widened or walked around. Food may be found. Smaller companions may walk where I can see them. Nearly every shortcoming is simply another thing to prepare for. I hope you remember that when you encounter one of your own.

Keep doing wel-

I found another pen. Several days have passed.

We reached a place where the stone was almost completely hidden beneath growth. Vines covered the walls and roots broke through the ground. Some of the plants moved when we approached them, although I do not know whether they were truly aware of us. There was an animal among them whose size nearly rivalled my own.
<>
Its back was covered in long thorns, and its body was broad enough to force the plants aside as it moved. I do not know what it is called. Its many legs pierced the ground and surrounding walls as it chewed through the terrain. Perhaps the humans gave it a name in one of their records. If so, they did not think we needed to know it.
<>
I had not realised how comforting it was to be the largest living thing nearby until I was not. It came through the growth and charged at the others. I placed myself between them and told them to run. One attempted to argue, but the rest pulled them away. When I heard their footsteps retreating, I felt proud. They trusted me to hold it. I did hold it. For longer than I thought possible.
<>
I broke several of its thorns against the stone and forced it away from the passage. It struck hard enough with its legs to knock me down, but I stood again. Each time it attacked, I believed the next attempt would be the one where I finally overpowered it.
<>
It eventually fled into the growth. I could not follow.

It took my left leg before it went.

I should be pleased that the others escaped. I am pleased. I would make the same decision again, even knowing what it would cost me.
<>
I am still angry that I could not kill it. It may find them again. It may find someone else. I was strong enough to drive it away, but not strong enough to ensure that nobody would ever need protection from it again. That does not feel like a victory.
<>
I have spent much of my journey appreciating my size. Now I find myself resenting it. I resent the passages I cannot enter and the routes which must be changed for me. I resent how much food it takes to keep me moving. Every portion I eat could sustain someone smaller for much longer. I resent that others see my strength and decide they are safe.
<>
When someone drops their belongings, I believe I should have carried them. When someone is injured, I wonder why I was not standing closer. When I arrive after something has already happened, I think of every moment in which I might have walked faster.
<>
Even minor things remain with me. A bruised shoulder caused by squeezing around me. A torn strap I pulled too firmly. A meal which ran short after I had eaten. The others likely forgot these things, but for whatever reason, I cannot.
<>
I know this is unfair. If another Baron spoke this way, I would remind them that strength does not make them responsible for every injury around them. I would tell them that every injury is still an injury, but it is not necessarily a failure.

But it is much easier to offer that kindness than to believe it.

Well, I appear to have ruined what was meant to be an encouraging note.
<>
This is not how I normally write, and it is not how I wish to speak to whoever finds me next. I think pain has allowed my thoughts to wander somewhere unhelpful. I will leave the note here. Perhaps leaving it behind will allow me to leave this mood with it. Please do not carry the latter half on my behalf.
<>
The beginning remains true. You found this note. You have made it this far. Whatever has frightened, injured or inconvenienced you has not taken that achievement away.

Continue carefully. Eat when you are able. Let others help you when they offer, even if you believe you are supposed to be the one helping them. I will attempt to remember that as well.

If we happen to meet, please do not mention how miserable I became. I would prefer the opportunity to introduce myself properly.

The project aimed to produce a Sawian with heritable shark traits, establish a living source of shark-derived tissue and assess practical applications after population stability had been achieved.

The final objective was deferred on the assumption that a viable aquatic carnivore would eventually prove useful.

Initial subjects were produced through cloning. Once reproductive viability was confirmed, growth continued through cloning and natural reproduction.

Like other Sawians, SAW-05 subjects are gonosimulistic and capable of asexual reproduction. They retain the characteristic absence of sex drive found throughout the Sawian population.
<>
SAW-05 nevertheless initiates reproduction more readily than most species. Individual development is not faster, however a greater proportion begins reproduction without prolonged encouragement.

Pain suppression is not, in itself, a novel phenomenon, and I want to establish that plainly before describing what this project actually did.

It occurs naturally, under the right circumstances, in essentially every species capable of feeling pain in the first place. An injury sustained in the middle of a genuine crisis is frequently not felt as an injury at all until well after the crisis has passed; the body, flooded with its own stress response, simply declines to prioritize the signal. This is not a defect. It is a functioning system doing exactly what it is meant to do under load.
<>
It is also achievable deliberately, and by relatively unsophisticated means. Chemical pain suppression, in various forms, has existed for as long as there have been substances capable of interrupting the relevant signaling, and its general principle is neither obscure nor proprietary to this project.

What this project was tasked with was neither of these things. It was not attempting to replicate an incidental stress response, and it was not attempting to formulate another substance to be administered externally, on a schedule, at a controlled dose.
<>
It was tasked with producing suppression that was internal, standing, and available to the subject on demand, without external intervention, at a level of effect neither of the above examples come close to. The mechanism this project settled on, and the one described here, operates through the same descending pain-control pathway responsible for the natural suppression described above, deliberately and directly engaged rather than triggered incidentally by crisis. The relevant circuit, seated in the lower brain and upper spinal relay, is capable of intercepting pain signaling before it reaches the point of full conscious registration. Under ordinary circumstances, this circuit engages briefly and involuntarily. What this project achieved was a subject capable of engaging it consciously, and holding it open, for as long as they choose to sustain it.

That is the achievement. It is also, inseparably, the problem.

The suppression circuit does not exist in isolation. In every subject examined, including outside this project entirely, its activation is accompanied by a corresponding rise in the body's stress-response output, the same general system responsible for elevated heart rate and blood pressure under acute threat. This is not incidental overlap. The two are bound together at a level beneath conscious control, in a manner this project was never able to fully separate, and I am no longer confident it can be separated using this pathway at all. Suppress the pain, and the stress response rises with it, for as long as the suppression is sustained.
<>
A brief engagement produces a brief, tolerable rise. The subject feels little beyond the intended effect. The difficulty is duration. The longer suppression is held, the longer the stress response is sustained alongside it, and the further heart rate departs from resting baseline the longer that state continues. This is a cumulative burden, not a fixed cost. A subject holding suppression for a short period experiences a manageable elevation. A subject holding it for a sustained period is, functionally, asking their own heart to sustain an emergency-level output for far longer than the body is designed to tolerate one.
<>
Past a certain duration, the heart does not simply tire. Sustained output at that level risks the destabilization of the heart's own electrical rhythm outright, a genuine and well-documented failure mode under prolonged severe stress, observed in unmodified physiology as well as in every subject line available to this project. When it occurs, the result is functional cardiac arrest. I want to be precise about what this means, because I believe it has been misunderstood by those reviewing this project from outside it: the heart is not damaged. It has not failed structurally. It has, in the overwhelming majority of documented instances, simply stopped, the way a system driven past its operating parameters stops, without necessarily being destroyed by the attempt.

This is why the condition has proven survivable as often as it has. A stopped heart with no structural injury can, in most cases, be restarted by ordinary means, manual or mechanical, and will resume ordinary function once restarted. It is not being repaired. It never needed repairing. It needed only to be told to continue.
<>
I will note, because it should be recorded plainly rather than left implied, that this does not make the event free of consequence. Each instance carries its own risk independent of the mechanism producing it, primarily through the interval of oxygen deprivation the body sustains while stopped. A subject may be restarted successfully six times and fail on the seventh not because the mechanism has changed, but because the cumulative toll of six prior events has left less margin than the first ever provided. The system does not become safer through repetition. It simply has not yet failed.

A secondary behavioral pattern emerged over the latter half of this project's operation, affecting a majority of subjects retained past the project's midpoint. The word itself, independent of context, independent even of whether suppression was being requested at the time, began producing involuntary response in affected subjects. The response was not consistent, which delayed identification considerably. In some subjects it produced withdrawal, a sudden and total disengagement from the immediate environment. THREE IN A LINE

We were given the original game in the lab. Nine squares, two players, three marks in a line to win. The humans used it to observe how we behaved towards one another.
<>
Among Milkies, it became tedious very quickly. We learnt the useful positions and the answers to them. Most games ended in a draw, with both players knowing how the rest would go several turns before it happened. Eventually the interesting part was seeing how long we could get away with staring blankly at the board before the observing human told us to continue.
<>
I kept a version for travelling. A few stones and some scratched lines made a pleasant distraction for companions who enjoyed it more than we had. There was nothing wrong with a simple game. I just didn't expect to get much out of playing it myself.

Latch, a Shelly we've been travelling with, took an interest while we were waiting for the others to finish repairs. I explained the rules. They watched my hands, examined the board and asked, in writing, whether I wanted the first turn. I offered it to them. I won anyways, which was unsurprising.
<>
They won the next game while I was explaining how to prevent exactly that sort of loss. I had been watching their hands rather than the board, which I pointed out. They moved their hands out of the way, but it didn't improve the following game.

It was irritating. I knew this game. I had been bored of it before Latch had probably seen a board, and here I was overlooking familiar positions because I had decided I would not need to pay attention.
<>
I suggested that we make it more interesting. Latch agreed immediately, which I thought was rather gracious until they slid the stones back towards me and waited with their pen ready.

I drew a larger board. Four squares along each side. We would have only four stones each, and once they were all placed, we could move them. Now the familiar little patterns would not be enough. A blocked line could become a different threat. There would be room to manoeuvre, and a reason to think beyond the opening. Choose to skip one of your turns, and you were allowed to place 1 bonus stone on your next.
<>
There was a bit of back and forth on clarifying rules. Diagonal lines still counted, and I had to write some of the new stuff down. Then Latch wanted me to redo the lines themselves because they weren't straight enough.
<>
The larger board helped. Unfortunately, it helped both of us. Latch began moving a stone backwards and forwards, inviting me to move the one blocking it. I refused. They waited. I moved something else to improve my position.

They ended up winning elsewhere.
<>
I said we needed a rule against immediately undoing a move. They considered that, then wrote, 'You could have left yours there.' I was aware of that NOW. We agreed to the new rule before starting again. I was not taking victories away from them or something, I just want to clarify.

By then an Experiment had come to watch. Latch made room by moving my bag rather than theirs. A second spectator arrived, and soon I was explaining the changes to everyone. One noticed a line I was preparing and became quite excited. I explained how it would force Latch to defend, allowing me to-
<>
Latch suddenly moved. There was a short silence. The Experiment asked if that was what I meant. It was not, they'd managed to slip their devious plans right past me. Latch tapped the board to remind me it was my turn.
<>
I had expected a calm, agreeable companion. They were agreeable about playing. About everything else, they had opinions. They wanted the better-lit seat. Two stones were too similar. My bag was in the way again. I was taking a long time for somebody who kept explaining what everybody ought to do. They were not simply enduring the game to keep me company. They wanted to win it.
<>
Once I accepted that, I started enjoying myself. I stopped delivering little lessons. Latch stopped prompting me to move. We took turns finding openings and spoiling them. The spectators followed some of it, missed some of it, and argued cheerfully over moves neither of us intended to make.
<>
I won a very close game. Latch studied the board, then held out a hand. I shook it. They wrote, 'That one was good.' It was. I wanted another before we had even collected the stones.
<>
We had to pack up instead. Latch offered to carry the pieces for another session, provided I stopped adding squares whenever I lost. I told them that had happened once. They held up one finger, then pointed to the four rows. I am choosing to believe that was a joke.

I don't think we have invented something that will keep every Milky occupied forever. We will learn its patterns too. But we had made something neither of us knew all the answers to yet, and Latch was an excellent person to discover them with. I had forgotten that part of playing.

So, here are the rules we actually agreed on. Try them with someone whose company you enjoy.
<>
RULES
1. Draw a board four squares wide and four squares tall. Each player needs FIVE recognisable pieces.
2. Take turns placing one piece in any empty square.
3. Once you both have FOUR of your pieces down, take turns moving one of your pieces into an empty square directly above, below or beside it. No jumping, pushing enemy pieces or moving diagonally.<>
4. Four of your pieces in an unbroken straight line wins, including diagonals. You can win during placement phase too.
5. A piece cannot return to the square it left on your previous turn. If you have no legal move, you lose.
6. You can spend one of your turns without moving at all to place your final piece in any unoccupied space on the board.
7. If the same positions keep repeating, agree to a draw and start again.
<>
You can instead play the simpler version, using a 3x3 board and placing pieces until one of you have 3 in a row or you run out of space, resulting in a tie.

Also, don't use food for pieces. That was a separate incident...
